centralClaimAdjudications.claim: THE CENTRAL CLAIM — no registry builder can receive the artifact, so an artifact-sized loop is unwritable; 0 artifact parameters, 0 artifact reads, 0 artifact-sized loops against 5 in the predecessor.
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: THE OUTCOME IS TRUE AND I COULD NOT DEFEAT IT. THE STATED MECHANISM IS NOT. registry_purity() is a naming lint, not a structural proof — it is TRUE-OF-WHAT-IT-INSPECTS. The class is nevertheless closed in the code as written, by three mechanisms, only one of which registry_purity measures.
centralClaimAdjudications.isRegistryPurityGenuinelyStructural: NO. measure() counts parameters whose name is literally `value`, call sites spelled `at(value,` or `resolves_in(value,`, and loops only where a name was FIRST bound by `X = at(value, …)` and then appears in a `for`. I wrote three builders that defeat it and measured its verdict on each: (1) `evil_registry(artifact, pinned)` — takes the artifact under the name `artifact`, subscripts it directly and sizes a loop from it: purity reports 0 parameters, 0 reads, 0 artifact-sized loops, completely invisible; (2) `evil2(value)` — reads via `value['knownLimitations']` subscript: 0 reads, 0 loops; (3) `evil3(value)` — `for i in range(len(at(value, …)))`, a genuine artifact-sized loop with no intermediate binding: artifactSizedLoops = 0. A lambda, an exec, a comprehension, a method or a decorator would fare the same, but none of those is needed — a different parameter name is sufficient.

canARegistryBeSizedIndirectly.throughDeps: YES IN PRINCIPLE, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. evidence_registry's declared signature is (deps, measured, audit, direction_preserved) and its docstring says it 'needs no artifact argument and cannot be sized by its subject'. That is FALSE as stated: `deps` IS value['decisionDependencies'], audit = measure_audit(deps, claims) is one row per dep, evidence_registry loops `for row in audit:` emitting 6 positions per row, and closure_registry loops `for row in m['audit']:` emitting 5 more. The registry IS artifact-sized through deps. What saves it is a mechanism registry_purity does not inspect and the artifact does not declare: line 1965 compares canon(deps) against the SHA-verified pinned predecessor's and, on any difference, emits VER11-DEP AND replaces deps with the pinned list BEFORE any registry is built. I verified this empirically — appending a decisionDependencies entry produces VER11-SURFACE + VER11-DEP at exit 1, and the registry does not grow. So the class is closed here by equality-gate-plus-fallback, not by purity.
canARegistryBeSizedIndirectly.throughMeasured: NO. `measured` is the D9 span, computed from two SHA-verified pinned contracts. Its list lengths are properties of d9-exit-contract v1.6 and v1.14, both in PINS.
canARegistryBeSizedIndirectly.throughAudit: Same as deps — audit is derived from deps and is safe only because deps is forced pinned-equal.
canARegistryBeSizedIndirectly.throughPinned: NO, and this is genuinely structural. frozen_registry(root, pinned) is sized by leaf_items() over the pinned predecessor block. PINS is verified unconditionally at the top of _check() — not gated by verify_files — so every pinned input's SHA-256 is checked on every call and a drifted predecessor returns VER11-PIN rather than a resized registry. I confirmed the verification is unconditional by reading the control flow.
canARegistryBeSizedIndirectly.throughTheRegister: NO. claim-register.v1.json is deliberately unpinned, but no registry loop is sized by `claims`; measure_audit iterates deps and rehearse() iterates a constant three variants. The register can change VALUES that are hard-compared, never POSITION COUNTS.

whatIsGenuinelyStructural: frozen_registry: sized from SHA-verified pinned bytes. Immune, and the strongest of the three.

closure_registry: sized from checker constants — REQUIRED_RESIDUAL_IDS, V11_REQUIRED_INPUTS, RESTATED_RESIDUALS, NOT_CLAIMED_TOKENS, PARTITION_SCOPES, DEMONSTRATIONS, the pattern tables — plus measurements. This is a real and complete repair of exactly the four loops B-VER10R-01 named: 45 + 22 + 8 + 4 = 79 positions now generated from constants.
evidence_registry: sized from deps/audit, made safe by the equality-gate-plus-fallback described above.
centralClaimAdjudications.adjudication: '0 artifact-sized loops' is true of the three functions inspected, under a definition keyed on one parameter name and two call spellings. It is not a proof that an artifact-sized loop is unwritable — I wrote three that score 0. A future editor who adds a builder taking the artifact under any other name, or who removes the line-1965 fallback while keeping evidence_registry's signature, would score a clean 0 on every purity counter and reintroduce B-VER10R-01 exactly. The declared numbers are honest measurements of what the instrument measures; the sentence 'it is not possible to write an artifact-sized loop in one' is an overstatement of what that measurement supports. NON-BLOCKING because the outcome holds for these bytes and I could not falsify it — but the reader should not treat registry_purity as the guarantee.

findings: The tolerance is NOT a licence to be red. The count itself is eq-compared: reg[...predecessorCheckerFindingsAgainstItsOwnBytes] = eqd(measured). So a repoint does not leave v11 silently green — it costs a declared leaf edit, which is precisely what my live rehearsal measured (0 -> 1). The tolerance suppresses only the VER11-PRED finding, not the accounting.

DIRECTION A, the predicted coupling: after my live repoint the predecessor emitted exactly one finding, at entries[6].registerBinding. VER11-PRED did NOT fire, predecessorRednessIsRegisterCoupledOnly stayed true, and the cost appeared as a countable leaf. Exactly as designed.

So a genuine predecessor defect is NOT admitted. I hit this accidentally and it is the cleanest possible confirmation.

The stated reason holds: without the tolerance, a coordinator repoint would make v11 permanently red through check-versioning-v10.py, which is frozen at 40e85b42… and which nobody may repair. Requiring silence from a frozen instrument coupled to a moving register would be the defect, not the guard.

nonBlockingObservations.title: registry_purity() is a naming lint, not a structural proof — 'unwritable' overstates 'unmeasured'.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: measure() counts only parameters literally named `value`, reads spelled `at(value,` or `resolves_in(value,`, and loops where a name was first bound by `X = at(value, …)`. I built three builders that defeat all three counters: a builder taking the artifact as `artifact` and subscripting it scores 0/0/0; a builder reading `value['k']` scores 0 reads; and `for i in range(len(at(value, …)))` — a genuine artifact-sized loop — scores 0 artifact-sized loops because there is no intermediate binding.
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: The declared numbers are honest measurements of what the instrument measures, and the outcome they report is true for these bytes. But the docstring's 'it is not possible to write an artifact-sized loop in one' is not supported by the measurement, and the counter most load-bearing to the central claim — artifactSizedLoops — has the narrowest pattern of the three. Counting by AST rather than by regex, or asserting the parameter TYPE rather than its name, would make the claim as strong as it reads.

nonBlockingObservations.title: evidence_registry DOES receive artifact-derived data; the class is closed there by an undeclared equality-gate-plus-fallback, not by purity.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: `deps` is value['decisionDependencies']; audit = measure_audit(deps, claims) is one row per dep; evidence_registry loops `for row in audit` at 6 positions per row and closure_registry loops `for row in m['audit']` at 5 more. Line 1965 compares canon(deps) against the pinned predecessor's and on any difference emits VER11-DEP and REPLACES deps with the pinned list before any registry is built. I confirmed empirically: appending a decisionDependencies entry gives VER11-SURFACE + VER11-DEP at exit 1 and the registry does not grow.
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: The protection is real and I could not get past it. But evidence_registry's docstring — 'this builder needs no artifact argument and cannot be sized by its subject' — is false as written, and the mechanism that actually protects it is not declared anywhere in the artifact and is not what registry_purity measures. A future editor who preserved the signature and dropped the fallback would score a clean 0 on every purity counter while reintroducing B-VER10R-01. Declaring the fallback as the guard, and comparing it, would put the real mechanism under the same discipline as everything else in this record.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The census assigns each leaf to its strongest gate, not its only gate; 432 leaves are double-gated and the byte-carry figure understates real coverage.

nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: NOT a defect and the error is in the safe direction — every one of the 432 is gated twice, and the partition claim 'assigned to exactly one gate' is true as stated because it describes an assignment, not an exclusivity of coverage. Recorded so that gatedByByteCarryAgainstThePredecessor: 148 is not read as the total byte-carried surface.
